transcript.text: LG F4V5VYP0W says OE and the clothes are sat in water. I'm not opening the little door at the bottom because last time I did that it flooded the whole kitchen. What else can I do?

OE means the washer has failed to drain. Don’t force the door open, and don’t keep restarting it repeatedly.

You can try these things without opening the lower filter flap:

1. Turn it off at the wall and unplug it for 5–10 minutes.
2. Check the large drain hose at the back:
• Make sure it isn’t kinked, crushed behind the machine, or bent sharply.
• Check that the end hasn’t been pushed too far down the standpipe/drain pipe.
• If it drains into a sink, check the sink trap/drain is not blocked.
3. Plug it back in and select Drain/Spin (or Spin with the spin speed selected), with no wash programme running.
• If you hear the pump humming but no water goes out, there is likely a blockage in the pump/filter or the drain hose.
• If it drains normally, let it finish, then the door should unlock.

If it still will not drain, the water has to be removed somehow before the clothes can be recovered. The least messy alternatives are:

• Wet/dry vacuum: Put the vacuum hose over/into the drain hose or use it to remove water once access is available.
• Use the rear drain hose into containers: With the machine switched off and unplugged, carefully take the drain hose out of its standpipe/sink connection and lower it into a very shallow tray or bucket. It may gravity-drain, so have several containers and towels ready. Raise the hose between swaps to stop the flow.
• Call an appliance engineer and tell them it has an OE drain error and is full of water. They can drain it safely and clear the pump/filter blockage.

Unfortunately, if the pump/filter is blocked, opening the lower flap is normally eventually necessary—but the key is to drain through the small emergency hose first, if your model has one, or use very shallow containers/towels rather than unscrewing the filter straight away. Do not unscrew the filter cap while the drum is still full of water.

Also, don’t tip the washing machine forward or on its side while it is full.

Right, the machine was pushed right back against the wall and the hose was squashed behind it, so I've pulled it out and straightened it. The kitchen sink is fine. I tried drain/spin again and it drained a bit slower than normal, then OE came up again. I'm still not unscrewing that filter, and I have towels and a baking tray if there's another way.

Yes — use the main drain hose at the back to empty it gradually into the baking tray. This avoids opening the filter.

1. Switch off and unplug the washer.
2. Put towels around the rear of the machine and have the baking tray ready.
3. Find where the washer’s grey/black drain hose enters the sink waste/standpipe.
4. Keep the hose raised upright while you free its end from the drain pipe — don’t lower it yet.
5. Put the hose end into the baking tray on the floor. Lowering it below the level of water in the drum should let water run out by gravity.

The tray will fill fast, so:

• When it is nearly full, lift the hose end above the level of the washer drum or pinch/kink the hose shut to stop the flow.
• Empty the tray into the sink.
• Put the hose back down and repeat until little or no water comes out.

A baking tray is shallow, but that is actually manageable if you do it in small batches. Keep the hose end under control at all times; don’t let it drop.

Once it has drained:

• Refit the hose securely into its normal drain connection, ensuring it is not squashed or sharply bent.
• Run Drain/Spin again.
• If it still gives OE after the drum is empty, it is likely a partial blockage in the pump/filter or drain hose, or a weak pump — but at least you can get the clothes out and avoid a flood.

If water only trickles from the rear hose even when it is on the floor, stop there: that suggests a blockage further inside the machine/hose, and an engineer is the sensible next step if you do not want to access the filter.

Do not pull the washer’s door open until the water has drained and it unlocks normally.
Hmm, a baking tray is really shallow and I've got laminate floor, so I'm worried that'll go everywhere like last time. Is there a less risky way to get the water out?

Yes: don’t use the baking tray. The lower-risk option is to use a proper bucket, washing-up bowl, mop bucket, or deep plastic storage box on the floor, with towels as backup.

You do not need to open the filter flap for this.

1. Switch off and unplug the machine.
2. Pull it forward only enough to access the rear drain hose — don’t tip it.
3. Put a deep container on the floor. A washing-up bowl is much safer than a tray; a 10 L bucket is better.
4. Keep the hose held upright while you take it out of the sink drain connection.
5. Put the hose end right down into the container, then lower it gradually.

If water starts running:

• Keep one hand on the hose.
• When the container is getting too full, lift the hose above the height of the drum (or pinch/kink it closed) to stop the flow.
• Empty the container into the sink and repeat.

A helper makes this much less stressful: one person controls the hose, the other empties the bucket.

If you have no suitable bucket/bowl, safer alternatives are:

• Borrow/buy a cheap mop bucket or 10–15 L builders’ bucket.
• Use a wet/dry vacuum to pull water through the rear drain hose or remove water from the drum once accessible.
• Call an appliance engineer; tell them it is showing OE, partially drained after a crushed hose, and still contains water.

Because it drained somewhat after you straightened the hose, there may be debris lodged in the pump/filter which has only partly cleared. Once you have safely emptied it through the rear hose, try Drain/Spin once more. If OE returns, don’t keep running it — it will likely need the filter/pump area cleared or the pump checked.
